title: Test your API step by step
summary: Run health, validation and real Oracle CRUD checks for the Reading List API. Use a repeatable test script and know what each test proves.
introduction: Testing means asking the app a question and checking the reply against what we expect. One happy request is not enough. We also try missing books, bad titles and the full create-read-update-delete journey.
learningObjectives: Separate a health check from a database integration test
Use the sample test script with a running Oracle database

items: Oracle is running and the sample table exists.
The connection secret belongs to reading_app in the right service.
The API is running on localhost:5080.
You are using only the separate learning database.

blocks.title: Run in a second terminal from the extracted sample root

blocks.text: Read the script before running it. It checks expected replies and uses a made-up book for its write tests. It should stop and report a failed check instead of printing a success message after a bad response. Its README describes the cleanup behaviour.

rows: The API can read the table.
A row was created and its ID returned.
The controller rejects an invalid ID.
blocks.caption: Important checks for this API

blocks.text: Look at the HTTP status yourself

blocks.code:
$body = @{ title = "Status Check Book"; isRead = $false } | ConvertTo-Json
$response = Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:5080/api/books `
  -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body -UseBasicParsing
$response.StatusCode
$response.Headers.Location
$book = $response.Content | ConvertFrom-Json
Invoke-RestMethod "http://localhost:5080/api/books/$($book.id)" -Method Delete
blocks.title: Inspect and clean up one POST

blocks.text: Invoke-RestMethod is handy for data. Invoke-WebRequest also gives you headers and the status. Both report HTTP errors; a failing request is useful evidence while testing.

A successful dotnet build checks that the C# code and packages fit together. A health test checks that the HTTP app starts. Neither one proves that Oracle accepted the SQL. Only the database checks, run against your real learning database, test that whole path.
Write down the result for three checks: health, invalid title and create-read-delete. If the database check fails, record the error type without copying the password or connection string.
